summary: Describes the URN Namespace Identifier etsi for identifying resources published by the European Telecommunications Standards Institute.

eli5.summary: A standards group gets its own prefix so its documents have permanent web-style names.

questions: what is the etsi urn namespace
what is a urn namespace identifier
subtitle: A permanent naming scheme for ETSI standards documents.

tldr.problem: ETSI, a major international standards organization, needed a way to create permanent, globally unique identifiers for the resources and documents it publishes.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8515 registers a formal URN Namespace Identifier (NID) called 'etsi', allowing ETSI to create identifiers like 'urn:etsi:yang:etsi-nfv' that are managed and guaranteed to be unique.
tldr.outcome: ETSI can now assign persistent, globally unique identifiers to all its published resources following a standardized scheme, with IANA registering the 'etsi' NID in the Formal URN Namespaces registry.

facts.label: Registrant Organization
facts.value: ETSI Protocol Naming and Numbering Service (PNNS)

today: RFC 8515 is an Informational RFC that has been registered with IANA. The 'etsi' Namespace Identifier is now part of the Formal URN Namespaces registry and is actively used by ETSI to assign persistent identifiers to its published specifications and resources.

sections.title: Introduction to URN Namespaces
sections.content:
ETSI (European Telecommunications Standards Institute) is an international standards organization that publishes specifications for information and communication technologies across many domains: fixed and mobile networks, radio, broadcast, internet and others.

Like other major standards bodies, ETSI needed a way to create persistent, globally unique identifiers for all the resources it publishes. This RFC registers a formal Uniform Resource Name (URN) Namespace Identifier called 'etsi' that allows ETSI to create identifiers following a standard format. A URN like 'urn:etsi:yang:etsi-nfv' serves as a permanent name that never changes, even if the physical location of the document changes.
sections.eli5: Imagine you want to give everything you make its own permanent name tag that won't change no matter where you move it. That's what a URN namespace does.

sections.title: URN Namespace Components
sections.content:
A URN has two main parts. The Namespace Identifier (NID) is the prefix, like 'etsi'. The Namespace Specific String (NSS) is everything after it, like 'yang:etsi-nfv' in the full URN 'urn:etsi:yang:etsi-nfv'.

The RFC specifies that ETSI's namespace is case-insensitive, so 'URN:ETSI:YANG:ETSI-NFV' and 'urn:etsi:yang:etsi-nfv' both refer to the same resource. The RFC follows the formal registration requirements defined in RFC 8141.
sections.eli5: The prefix 'etsi' is the first part, like your first name. The rest is specific to each resource, like your last name and address.

sections.title: How ETSI Manages the Namespace
sections.content:
ETSI maintains a registry of subtrees that use the 'etsi' NID at its Protocol Naming and Numbering Service (PNNS). When ETSI assigns a subtree (like 'yang' for YANG data models), that assignment cannot later be deleted or reassigned to something else, ensuring stability.

ETSI may permit secondary responsibility for certain defined resources and may allow experimental namespace values for testing, following the guidance in RFC 6963. Once a subtree assignment is made to a particular purpose, it remains dedicated to that purpose permanently.
sections.eli5: ETSI keeps a list of all the different types of things it names, and once it decides that 'yang' means data models, that meaning stays forever.

sections.title: Examples of ETSI URNs
sections.content: The RFC provides examples of URNs that ETSI might assign: 'urn:etsi:yang:etsi-nfv', 'urn:etsi:yang:etsi-nfv-vnf' and 'urn:etsi:yang:etsi-nfv-pnf'. These examples are all related to network management using YANG, a data modeling language. The RFC notes that while these examples focus on YANG, ETSI may in the future create URNs with different sub-identifiers for other types of resources.
sections.eli5: For example, ETSI might say 'urn:etsi:yang:etsi-nfv' is the permanent name for the NFV (network function virtualization) data model.

sections.title: Security and Considerations
sections.content: The RFC notes that there are no additional security considerations beyond those normally associated with URNs in general, as described in RFC 1737 and RFC 8141. The main benefit is that by having a stable, persistent naming scheme, downstream users can rely on the names staying the same, making systems more robust.
sections.eli5: Using permanent names is actually safer because programs can rely on those names never disappearing.
